name: issue_858_comfort_family_reactive_floor_breach
description: Issue #858 / #1066 (Design D nearest-edge arming, docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md section 6f). The comfort-family selector must run reactively on each thermostat temperature tick, not only on the ~30-minute classification cycle. Live-incident shape: warm day, the scenario's ONLY classification event is at 06:00, indoor then falls below comfort_heat (68F) via temp_update events alone. The first reading below the floor (06:15, 67F) must arm heat immediately (floor breach, no deadband, sustain or recency wait), so the switch lands by 06:15.
notes: Occupant impact: on a live 2-zone install indoor fell from 67F to 62F (6F below the 68F floor) over 2h40m overnight before heat engaged, because the family decision only re-evaluated on apply_classification()'s ~30-minute cycle. The sleeping occupant must get heat on the first reading below the floor.

What this proves: only ONE classification event exists (06:00); the switch to heating must come from the reactive path (coordinator._async_thermostat_changed -> comfort_family_temperature_check() -> apply_classification()) on the 06:15 temp_update. The assertion time bounds are the first breach reading itself (06:15). Before Design D the same reading only armed a candidate (deadband, recency, 90 s sustain across two evaluations), so a bound of 06:15 could not have been met.

Baseline fix (Issue #1066 review): the original baseline sat inside the heat zone (indoor <= floor + m), so heat was already armed before the breach and the final-state assertions passed vacuously. The baseline is now inside the cooling zone so the breach reading is the first thing that can arm heat. (Heat zone is indoor <= 70F here; 70F at baseline would have armed heat at 06:00.)
Design D rule exercised (docs/08 section 6f): indoor < floor -> heating immediately, ignoring the 600 s dwell lock; the day type is not an input. The reactive check runs on every temperature change.
Classification fields: day_type=warm with hvac_mode=off, windows_recommended=false are what classifier.py derives for DAY_TYPE_WARM (Issue #867 rule: never hand-set hvac_mode=cool here).

(a) Scenario effectiveness: removing the coordinator._async_thermostat_changed wiring (or the comfort_family_temperature_check() call) fails the scenario, since no later classification event re-runs apply_classification(). With nearest-edge arming deleted (origin/main comfort_family_decision.py) a warm day is natively cooling; heat is the against-grain direction and needs a breach beyond the warm deadband, a recency check and a 90 s sustain across two evaluations, so the first breach reading (06:15) at most arms a candidate and comfort_family_switch_by(heating, 06:15), comfort_family=heating and last_hvac_mode=heat all fail.
(b) Docs<->production alignment: docs/08 section 6f 'Reactive evaluation' (every temperature change; breach switches immediately) and the rule row 'indoor < floor -> heating'.

(c) Occupant outcome if this test fails to catch a regression: the household sleeps in a house drifting below the comfort floor with the AC armed and no furnace for up to 30 minutes per missed cycle, as in the live incident.

events.note: Warm-day classification (hvac_mode=off, as classifier.py derives for DAY_TYPE_WARM). The ONLY classification event in the scenario; everything after is driven by temp_update alone.
Indoor 72F: inside the band [68F, 74F] and at ceiling - m (74 - 2 = 72F), the cooling zone, so cool is armed at 74. No breach yet.
First reading below the floor: 67F, 1F below comfort_heat(68). Floor breach: the reactive check arms heat on this very reading.

assertions.reason: Baseline: warm day, indoor within band -- comfort band arms normally at the ceiling.
Issue #858 / #1066: the switch to heating lands on the first breach reading (06:15), 15 minutes after the scenario's only classification event, driven entirely by the reactive temperature-tick path.
Final engine state confirms heating is armed, not merely an emitted event.
The commanded mode is a real climate service call at comfort_heat, not merely an internal flag.

verdict.summary: A floor breach arms heat on the first reactive temperature tick, without waiting for a second scheduled classification cycle (Issue #858, tightened for Issue #1066).
verdict.observed_behavior: Single classification event at 06:00 (warm/off); the 67F reading at 06:15 switches the family to heating and commands heat.
verdict.expected_behavior: Every current_temperature tick re-evaluates the nearest-edge selector; below the floor means heat immediately.
